title: One Question Each · Together
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play One Question Each · Together with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: The lead writes a familiar object on a hidden slip. Every other player asks one yes-or-no question; with two players, the partner may ask three. The group identifies the object after the questions. Play eight turns in total, rotating the lead. The group wins together if at least five turns succeed.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 2–8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In One Question Each, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The group identifies the object after the questions.
recall.why: The group identifies the object after the questions.
